'''Martin Zwierlein''' is a German physicist who is a professor of physics at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], Principal Investigator at the [[Research Laboratory of Electronics]], and an elected fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=apsref/><ref name=mitref/>

== Education and career ==
Zwierlein was educated at the [[University of Bonn]] and the [[École Normale Supérieure]].<ref name=mitref/> He obtained his Ph.D. at [[MIT]] under [[Wolfgang Ketterle]]. Afterwards, he was briefly a postdoctoral research associate in the group of [[Immanuel Bloch]] at [[Mainz University]].<ref name=bonnref/>

Zwierlein joined the [[MIT]] department of physics in 2007 and was promoted to full professor in 2013.<ref name=bonnref/>

He is a pioneer in the study of ultracold atomic Fermi gases and molecules. 

He was won numerous awards for his work, including the [[I. I. Rabi Prize]] of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2017,<ref name="iiprize"/> and the [[TOPTICA]] BEC Junior Award in 2021<ref name='bec2021'/>
